_doc: The items of Ruth's backpack and of the containers (INV-CORE, docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-09-inventory-design.md; the logic is scripts/sim/inventory.gd, the sim part scripts/town/inv.gd). Every number of the inventory is here. items: for each id the name, size (w by h cells, before a turn), stack (the most items in ONE placement: a placement covers its w by h cells whatever its count, so shells with stack 24 are 24 rounds in one cell and a bottle, stack 1, is two cells for one bottle), res (the store resource it stands for: ammo, food, water or meds), units (store units ONE item stands for: a ration pack is 3 food), use (eat, drink, bandage or none), desc (the tooltip). One unit of ammo is what the stores call a round: a shotgun shot costs 0.34 of it (sim.gd SHELL_COST), so a loose shell is worth about three shots; the reload takes whole units from the pack and keeps the fraction as a credit (inv.gd), so the economy the lab was tuned on does not move. pack: the backpack's grid. containers: the grid of a container by its kind (the generator's kinds and the street's cars), `default` for a kind not named; a grid grows by rows if the loot placed in it does not fit (never in the generator's own towns: tests/test_inventory.gd checks seeds 1 to 16). convert: how a container's loot units (the generator's `loot` {res: n}, unchanged) become items, for each res a list of [item, chance] tried in order while the units left are at least the item's: the plain unit item (units 1) takes the rest. withdraw: the items a withdrawn unit of a res is made of, the biggest first (a stack of canned food is the smallest way to carry food). needs (PH10, food and water): using an item whose `use` is eat or drink takes ONE store unit out of the pack (a ration pack or a jug is broken: the rest of its units go back as tins and bottles) and starts her hunger or thirst clock again (scripts/town/inv.gd `use_item`; a served meal at the base does the same); eat_min_h and drink_min_h are the game hours since the last proper meal or drink under which she is not hungry or thirsty enough to use one (the item is kept). The clocks themselves, and what hunger and thirst cost, are scripts/sim/supplies.gd's (hungry at 18 hours, thirsty at 14, health lost from 36 and 24). reveal_s: seconds between two items of a container showing in the loot window while it is searched. close_tiles: the window closes when she is farther from the container than this. drop_reach: how far from her feet a dropped pile lies.

shells.desc: Shotgun shells. The reload takes them from the pack.

canned_food.name: Canned food
canned_food.desc: A tin of food: one ration, enough for most of a day.

ration_pack.name: Ration pack
ration_pack.desc: A pack of dried rations: three rations. Eating one leaves two tins.

water_bottle.name: Water bottle
water_bottle.desc: A bottle of clean water: one drink, good for half a day.

water_jug.name: Water jug
water_jug.desc: A jug of clean water: four bottles' worth. A drink leaves three bottles.

parts_box.name: Parts box
parts_box.desc: Electronics, pump and generator pieces. Spent on projects at the base.

fuel_can.name: Fuel can
fuel_can.desc: A can of fuel: a day for the generator.
